page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It provisions 90 dedicated vCPUs spanning 45 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 360 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory allocation. The hardware features 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside specialized vector instructions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. The instance includes 3216 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across eight drives, without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong aggregate multi-core computational throughput and fast I/O processing. The instance scores in the top decile on the PassMark CPU test (87474.41), CPU extended instructions (115295.02), and Clang software compilation benchmarks (59916.0). Memory performance yields small-block cached read throughput of 6372.53 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads of 217.44 GB/sec, although write operations settle into average performance tiers at 76.89 GB/sec. Data-intensive workloads benefit from strong operations per second, reaching 117.73 million Redis SET operations per second and high static web serving throughput of 56.29 GB/sec.

With its dedicated high-vCPU footprint and high-capacity local NVMe array, the instance achieves high resource density for disk-bound and distributed compute tasks. The integration of 3.2 TB local NVMe storage provides low-latency ephemeral I/O without incurring external block storage overhead, though lack of discrete GPU hardware precludes high-throughput machine learning model generation. This configuration is well matched for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, large-scale software compilation, distributed caching, and static web serving tiers.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90-lssd is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 90 dedicated vCPUs and 360 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The server integrates 3216 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across eight drives, delivering substantial ephemeral I/O capacity without discrete GPU hardware. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 vector extensions and dedicated hardware cryptographic acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing metrics, with leading scores in PassMark CPU tests, extended instruction sets, and large-scale Clang software compilation. Memory bandwidth reaches 217.44 GB/sec for uncached reads, supporting high transaction rates with 117.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 56.29 GB/sec static web throughput. This architecture provides high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads, making it appropriate for distributed database hosting, caching layers, continuous integration compilation clusters, and high-volume web serving.
